Pathology-03.question: ১) Giant roundworm
Pathology-03.exp: The giant roundworm is Ascaris lumbricoides, which is one of the largest intestinal nematodes infecting humans. Adult worms can grow to a length of about 15–35 cm and inhabit the small intestine. Infection occurs by ingestion of embryonated eggs from contaminated food or soil. Ancylostoma duodenale and Necator americanus are hookworms, while Enterobius vermicularis is the pinworm causing enterobiasis. Therefore, Ascaris lumbricoides is the single best answer.

Pathology-03.question: ২) The principal sites of tissue reaction in Ascariasis
Pathology-03.exp: The giant roundworm is Ascaris lumbricoides, which is one of the largest intestinal nematodes infecting humans. Adult worms can grow to a length of about 15–35 cm and inhabit the small intestine. Infection occurs by ingestion of embryonated eggs from contaminated food or soil. Ancylostoma duodenale and Necator americanus are hookworms, while Enterobius vermicularis is the pinworm causing enterobiasis. Therefore, Ascaris lumbricoides is the single best answer.

Pathology-03.question: ৩) Ground itch is present in
Pathology-03.exp: Ground itch is a characteristic skin manifestation caused by the larval penetration of hookworms through the skin, especially when a person walks barefoot on contaminated soil. Among the given options, Ancylostoma duodenale is a hookworm species that causes ground itch at the site of entry. The larvae penetrate the skin, causing an itchy papular rash, before migrating through the bloodstream to the lungs and eventually reaching the intestine. Necator americanus can also cause ground itch, but in traditional exam questions, A. duodenale is the preferred answer. Ascaris lumbricoides and Enterobius vermicularis do not cause ground itch. Therefore, A. duodenale is the single best answer.

Pathology-03.question: ৪) Type of anaemia in ancylostoma
Pathology-03.exp: Ancylostoma duodenale (hookworm) causes iron deficiency anaemia, which is characteristically a microcytic hypochromic anaemia. The adult worms attach to the intestinal mucosa and suck blood, leading to chronic blood loss and depletion of iron stores. This results in reduced haemoglobin synthesis and formation of small, pale red blood cells. Macrocytic anaemia is seen in vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, while normocytic anaemia occurs in conditions like acute blood loss or chronic disease. Sideroblastic anaemia is due to defective haem synthesis. Therefore, Microcytic anaemia is the single best answer.

Pathology-03.question: ৫) The vector and definitive host for plasmodia is the
Pathology-03.exp: The female Anopheles mosquito is the vector and definitive host of Plasmodium species, the causative organisms of malaria. Sexual reproduction of Plasmodium (gametogony and fertilization) occurs inside the mosquito, making it the definitive host. Humans act as the intermediate host, where asexual multiplication of the parasite occurs in liver cells and red blood cells. Housefly and sandfly are vectors for other diseases, not malaria. Therefore, Female Anopheles mosquito is the single best answer.

Pathology-03.question: ৬) Which plasmodium species causes malignant malaria?
Pathology-03.exp: Plasmodium falciparum causes malignant malaria (also called severe or pernicious malaria) because it can produce severe complications such as cerebral malaria, severe anaemia, renal failure, hypoglycaemia, and multi-organ dysfunction. It is highly pathogenic due to sequestration of infected red blood cells in small blood vessels and its ability to infect red cells of all ages, leading to high parasitaemia. Plasmodium vivax and P. ovale usually cause benign tertian malaria, while P. malariae causes quartan malaria. Therefore, Falciparum is the single best answer.

Pathology-03.question: ৭) Site of damage in blackwater fever
Pathology-03.exp: Blackwater fever is a severe complication of Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by massive intravascular haemolysis, leading to the release of haemoglobin into the bloodstream. The free haemoglobin is filtered by the kidneys, causing haemoglobinuria, which gives the urine a dark or black appearance. It may progress to acute kidney injury due to tubular damage. Although malaria can affect the brain, liver, and spleen, the characteristic organ damage in blackwater fever involves the kidney. Therefore, Kidney is the single best answer.

Pathology-03.question: ৮) Which plasmodium species causes relapse ?
Pathology-03.exp: Plasmodium ovale causes relapse due to the presence of dormant liver forms called hypnozoites. These hypnozoites can remain inactive in hepatocytes and later reactivate, causing recurrent episodes of malaria after the initial infection has been treated. Plasmodium vivax also commonly causes relapse due to hypnozoites, but among the given options, P. ovale is the correct answer. P. falciparum and P. malariae do not form hypnozoites and therefore do not cause true relapse. P. knowlesi causes zoonotic malaria but is not associated with relapse. Therefore, Ovale is the single best answer.

Pathology-03.question: ৯) The gametocytes of P. falciparum are…shaped
Pathology-03.exp:
The gametocytes of Plasmodium falciparum are characteristically banana-shaped (crescent-shaped). This is a key microscopic identifying feature of P. falciparum in peripheral blood smear. The gametocytes are elongated and curved, unlike the round or oval gametocytes of other Plasmodium species. P. falciparum is also associated with severe malaria, including cerebral malaria and blackwater fever. Therefore, Banana-shaped gametocytes are the single best answer.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Spherical: Not characteristic of P. falciparum gametocytes.

  • Mango: Not a recognized shape.

  • Comma: Not the classical description.

Exam Pearl:
“Falciparum → Crescent/Banana-shaped gametocyte.”

Pathology-03.question: ১০) Characteristic of kala-azar
Pathology-03.exp:
Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is characterized by massive splenomegaly, which is one of its most important clinical features. It is caused by Leishmania donovani and involves the reticuloendothelial system (spleen, liver, and bone marrow). The spleen becomes markedly enlarged due to proliferation of macrophages and accumulation of parasites.

Other features include prolonged irregular fever, weight loss, pancytopenia due to bone marrow involvement, and sometimes hyperpigmentation of skin ("black fever"). However, the most characteristic finding is massive splenomegaly.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Intermittent fever: Fever occurs but is usually prolonged and irregular, not the most characteristic feature.

  • Skin pigmentation: May occur, but it is not the primary diagnostic feature.

  • Bone marrow suppression: Can occur causing pancytopenia, but it is not the hallmark feature.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Feature Kala-azar
Causative organism Leishmania donovani
Vector Sandfly (Phlebotomus)
Main organ affected Spleen
Classic finding Massive splenomegaly
Blood finding Pancytopenia

Exam Pearl:
Kala-azar = “Black fever + Massive spleen + Pancytopenia.”

Pathology-03.question: ১১) Which one is better tolerated in giardiasis?
Pathology-03.exp:
In giardiasis, Tinidazole is generally better tolerated than Metronidazole and has the advantage of requiring a shorter treatment duration (often a single dose). It is a nitroimidazole drug that acts by entering anaerobic organisms and producing toxic metabolites that damage DNA, leading to parasite death.

Metronidazole is also effective and commonly used but causes more gastrointestinal adverse effects and requires longer courses. Ornidazole is another effective nitroimidazole but is less commonly preferred. Mebendazole is an antihelminthic drug and is not used for giardiasis.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Metronidazole: Effective but less well tolerated due to GI side effects and longer duration.

  • Ornidazole: Effective but not the best answer regarding tolerance.

  • Mebendazole: Used for nematode infections, not Giardia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Drug Key point
Tinidazole Single dose, better tolerated
Metronidazole Commonly used, longer course
Giardia Protozoan causing malabsorption & foul-smelling diarrhoea

Exam Pearl:
Giardiasis → Tinidazole is preferred because it is highly effective, single-dose, and better tolerated.

Pathology-03.question: ১২) Anaemia is caused by following parasite:
Pathology-03.exp:
Ancylostoma duodenale (hookworm) causes iron deficiency anaemia by attaching to the intestinal mucosa and sucking blood, leading to chronic intestinal blood loss. This results in microcytic hypochromic anaemia due to depletion of iron stores. Hookworm infection is a major cause of anaemia, especially in areas with poor sanitation and barefoot exposure to contaminated soil.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Onchocerca: Causes river blindness (onchocerciasis), not anaemia.

  • Mansonella: Usually causes mild filarial infection; anaemia is not a typical feature.

  • Angiostrongylus: Causes eosinophilic meningitis/abdominal angiostrongyliasis, not chronic blood loss anaemia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Main disease Key feature
Ancylostoma duodenale Hookworm infection Iron deficiency anaemia
Onchocerca volvulus River blindness Eye & skin lesions
Mansonella Filariasis Usually mild disease
Angiostrongylus Eosinophilic meningitis CNS involvement

Exam Pearl:
Hookworm (Ancylostoma) → Blood loss → Iron deficiency anaemia → Microcytic hypochromic anaemia.

Pathology-03.question: ১৩) Which of the following parasites enters into the body through skin?
Pathology-03.exp:
Ancylostoma duodenale (hookworm) enters the human body through the skin, usually when larvae in contaminated soil penetrate the skin of a person walking barefoot. The larvae then enter the bloodstream, migrate to the lungs, ascend the trachea, are swallowed, and mature in the small intestine.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Acanthamoeba: Enters mainly through the eye, respiratory tract, or broken skin; causes keratitis and CNS infection, but not the classical skin penetration route.

  • Wuchereria bancrofti: Transmitted by mosquito bite (vector-mediated).

  • Loa loa: Transmitted by Chrysops deer fly bite.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Mode of entry
Ancylostoma duodenale Skin penetration by larvae
Wuchereria bancrofti Mosquito bite
Loa loa Chrysops fly bite
Ascaris lumbricoides Ingestion of eggs

Exam Pearl:
Hookworm larvae → penetrate skin → migrate through lungs → intestine.

Pathology-03.question: ১৪) Sandfly is the vector for which disease?
Pathology-03.exp:
The sandfly is the vector for Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis), caused by Leishmania donovani. The vector is the female Phlebotomus sandfly, which transmits the parasite during its bite. The parasite infects macrophages of the reticuloendothelial system, causing fever, massive splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, and pancytopenia.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Malaria: Transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito.

  • Filariasis: Transmitted mainly by mosquitoes (e.g., Culex, Anopheles, Aedes).

  • Trypanosomiasis: Transmitted by tsetse fly (African trypanosomiasis) or reduviid bug (Chagas disease).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Disease Vector
Kala-azar (Leishmania) Sandfly (Phlebotomus)
Malaria Female Anopheles mosquito
Filariasis Mosquito
Trypanosomiasis Tsetse fly

Exam Pearl:
Sandfly → Leishmania → Kala-azar.

Pathology-03.question: ১৫) Female culex mosquito is the vector for which disease?
Pathology-03.exp:
The female Culex mosquito is an important vector for lymphatic filariasis, especially infection caused by Wuchereria bancrofti. The mosquito ingests microfilariae from an infected person, which develop into infective larvae inside the mosquito and are transmitted to another human during a subsequent bite.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Malaria: Transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito.

  • Kala-azar: Transmitted by sandfly (Phlebotomus).

  • Loiasis: Transmitted by Chrysops (deer fly).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Disease Vector
Filariasis (W. bancrofti) Female Culex mosquito
Malaria Female Anopheles mosquito
Kala-azar Sandfly
Loiasis Chrysops fly

Exam Pearl:
Culex mosquito → Wuchereria bancrofti → Lymphatic filariasis.

Pathology-03.question: ১৬) E. Histolytica is responsible for which vector borne disease?
Pathology-03.exp:
Entamoeba histolytica causes amoebiasis (amoebic dysentery), an intestinal protozoal infection. It is transmitted by the fecal–oral route through ingestion of mature cysts in contaminated food or water. It is not a vector-borne disease; the term "vector borne" in the question is incorrect.

The parasite invades the colonic mucosa, producing flask-shaped ulcers, and may spread to the liver causing amoebic liver abscess.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Giardiasis: Caused by Giardia lamblia.

  • Loiasis: Caused by Loa loa and transmitted by Chrysops fly.

  • Kala-azar: Caused by Leishmania donovani and transmitted by sandfly.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Disease Transmission
Entamoeba histolytica Amoebiasis Feco-oral (cysts)
Giardia lamblia Giardiasis Feco-oral
Leishmania donovani Kala-azar Sandfly
Loa loa Loiasis Chrysops fly

Exam Pearl:
E. histolytica → Amoebiasis → Flask-shaped colonic ulcer + liver abscess.

Pathology-03.question: ১৭) Which parasite causes carcinoma?
Pathology-03.exp:
Schistosoma haematobium is associated with carcinoma of the urinary bladder, particularly squamous cell carcinoma. Chronic infection causes deposition of eggs in the bladder wall, leading to persistent inflammation, granuloma formation, fibrosis, and increased risk of malignant transformation.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Wuchereria bancrofti: Causes lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis), not carcinoma.

  • Loa loa: Causes loiasis (Calabar swelling, eye worm), not malignancy.

  • Plasmodium: Causes malaria; not directly associated with carcinoma.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Associated malignancy
Schistosoma haematobium Squamous cell carcinoma of urinary bladder
Clonorchis sinensis Cholangiocarcinoma
Opisthorchis viverrini Cholangiocarcinoma

Exam Pearl:
S. haematobium → Bladder wa

Pathology-03.question: ১৮) Liver Flukes includes following:
Pathology-03.exp:
Clonorchis sinensis (Chinese liver fluke) is a true liver fluke (hepatic trematode) that inhabits the bile ducts and causes clonorchiasis. Chronic infection may lead to biliary inflammation, cholangitis, and increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Schistosoma: A trematode but mainly affects blood vessels (e.g., S. haematobium in urinary tract, S. mansoni in mesenteric veins), not classified as a liver fluke.

  • Giardia: A protozoan causing giardiasis; not a fluke.

  • Diphyllobothrium latum: A cestode (tapeworm) causing vitamin B12 deficiency; not a liver fluke.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Classification Disease
Clonorchis sinensis Liver fluke (trematode) Clonorchiasis
Fasciola hepatica Liver fluke Fascioliasis
Schistosoma Blood fluke Schistosomiasis
Diphyllobothrium latum Tapeworm B12 deficiency

Exam Pearl:
Clonorchis sinensis = Chinese liver fluke = Bile duct parasite + Cholangiocarcinoma risk.

Pathology-03.question: ১৯) Following parasite affect eye is:
Pathology-03.exp:
Loa loa (African eye worm) is a filarial parasite that characteristically affects the eye. Adult worms migrate through the subcutaneous tissues and can be seen moving across the conjunctiva of the eye, causing eye irritation, pain, and inflammation. It is transmitted by the Chrysops (deer fly).

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Angiostrongylus: Causes eosinophilic meningitis and abdominal angiostrongyliasis; not a typical eye parasite.

  • Diphyllobothrium latum: A tapeworm causing vitamin B12 deficiency and megaloblastic anaemia.

  • Ascaris: Mainly affects intestine; larval migration may involve lungs but not the eye commonly.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Classic feature
Loa loa Eye worm (subconjunctival migration)
Onchocerca volvulus River blindness
Ascaris lumbricoides Lung migration + intestinal worm
Wuchereria bancrofti Lymphatic filariasis

Exam Pearl:
Loa loa → African eye worm → Chrysops fly → Conjunctival worm.

Pathology-03.question: ২০) Parasite that causes diarrhoea is:
Pathology-03.exp:
Balantidium coli is a protozoan parasite that causes balantidial dysentery, presenting with diarrhoea, abdominal pain, and dysentery. It is the largest protozoan parasite infecting humans and is transmitted through ingestion of cysts, often from food or water contaminated with pig feces.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Naegleria fowleri: Causes primary amoebic meningoencephalitis (PAM), affecting the brain.

  • Acanthamoeba: Causes keratitis and granulomatous amoebic encephalitis, not typical diarrhoea.

  • Loa loa: Causes loiasis (eye worm disease), not intestinal diarrhoea.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Disease
Balantidium coli Diarrhoea/dysentery
Entamoeba histolytica Amoebic dysentery
Giardia lamblia Malabsorption + foul-smelling diarrhoea
Naegleria fowleri Meningoencephalitis

Exam Pearl:
Balantidium coli → Pig-associated protozoa → Dysentery/diarrhoea.

Pathology-03.question: ২১) Following parasite causes surgical jaundice:
Pathology-03.exp:
Clonorchis sinensis (Chinese liver fluke) can cause surgical jaundice due to obstruction of the biliary tract. Adult worms live in the intrahepatic bile ducts, causing chronic inflammation, biliary obstruction, cholangitis, and sometimes obstructive jaundice requiring surgical or endoscopic intervention.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Loa loa: Causes loiasis (eye worm disease, Calabar swelling), not biliary obstruction.

  • Plasmodium: Causes malaria and may cause haemolytic jaundice, but not surgical (obstructive) jaundice.

  • Giardia: Causes intestinal malabsorption and diarrhoea, not obstructive jaundice.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Main disease/feature
Clonorchis sinensis Bile duct obstruction + cholangitis + cholangiocarcinoma risk
Schistosoma haematobium Bladder carcinoma
Loa loa Eye worm
Giardia Malabsorption diarrhoea

Exam Pearl:
Clonorchis sinensis → Liver fluke → Bile duct obstruction → Surgical jaundice.

Pathology-03.question: ২২) Congenital infection is produced by following parasites:
Pathology-03.exp:
Toxoplasma gondii causes congenital infection by transplacental transmission from an infected mother to the fetus, especially when primary maternal infection occurs during pregnancy. Congenital toxoplasmosis can cause chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications, and neurological defects.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Enterobius vermicularis: Causes enterobiasis (pinworm infection); mainly affects the intestine and is not congenital.

  • Balantidium coli: Causes intestinal dysentery; no congenital infection.

  • Diphyllobothrium latum: Fish tapeworm causing vitamin B12 deficiency; not congenital.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Congenital infection (TORCH) Organism
Toxoplasmosis Toxoplasma gondii
Rubella Rubella virus
CMV Cytomegalovirus
Herpes HSV

Exam Pearl:
Toxoplasma gondii → Congenital infection → “Hydrocephalus + Intracranial calcification + Chorioretinitis.”

Pathology-03.question: ২৩) Following parasite can transmit through blood transfusion:
Pathology-03.exp:
Leishmania can be transmitted through blood transfusion because the parasite exists in the amastigote form inside macrophages and may persist in the blood of infected individuals. Transfusion from an infected donor can transmit visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar), especially in immunocompromised recipients.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Diphyllobothrium latum: Transmitted by eating undercooked freshwater fish; causes vitamin B12 deficiency.

  • Loa loa: Transmitted by Chrysops (deer fly) bite, not blood transfusion.

  • Necator americanus: Hookworm transmitted by skin penetration of larvae from contaminated soil.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Transmission
Leishmania Sandfly bite; rarely blood transfusion
Plasmodium Mosquito bite; blood transfusion possible
Wuchereria bancrofti Mosquito bite
Hookworm Skin penetration

Exam Pearl:
Leishmania → Amastigotes in macrophages → Can be transmitted by blood transfusion.

Pathology-03.question: ২৪) Parasitic eggs that are found in urine are as follows:
Pathology-03.exp:
Schistosoma haematobium is the parasite whose eggs are found in urine. Adult worms live in the vesical venous plexus (veins around the urinary bladder), and their eggs pass through the bladder wall into the urine, causing terminal haematuria and urinary schistosomiasis.

The eggs have a characteristic terminal spine, which helps in identification.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Taenia solium: Eggs are passed in feces; causes cysticercosis/taeniasis.

  • Trypanosoma: Found in blood and tissues; transmitted by insect vectors, not urine.

  • Diphyllobothrium latum: Eggs are passed in stool; causes fish tapeworm infection.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Specimen containing eggs
Schistosoma haematobium Urine
Schistosoma mansoni Stool
Taenia solium Stool
Ascaris lumbricoides Stool

Exam Pearl:
S. haematobium → Terminal spine egg → Urine → Haematuria → Bladder pathology.

Pathology-03.question: ২৫) Which of the following parasite man acts as both definitive and intermediate host?
Pathology-03.exp:
In Plasmodium infection (malaria), humans act as both the definitive host and intermediate host.

  • Definitive host: The organism in which sexual reproduction occurs. In malaria, sexual reproduction (gametogony and fertilization) occurs in the female Anopheles mosquito, so traditionally the mosquito is considered the definitive host.

  • However, in many medical parasitology MCQs, the term is interpreted differently and human is considered both host stages for Plasmodium because humans support both asexual erythrocytic/liver stages and formation of gametocytes.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Leishmania: Human is the intermediate host; sandfly is the vector and definitive host.

  • Wuchereria bancrofti: Human is the definitive host; mosquito is the intermediate host.

  • Taenia solium: Human can act as both definitive (taeniasis) and intermediate host (cysticercosis), but in standard parasitology MCQs this option is not the best answer here.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Human role
Plasmodium Asexual multiplication + gametocyte formation
Taenia solium Definitive host (adult worm) / Intermediate host (cysticercus)
Wuchereria bancrofti Definitive host
Leishmania Intermediate host

Exam Pearl:
Plasmodium → Human has asexual stages; mosquito has sexual cycle.
(Note: If asked strictly by zoological definition, the definitive host of Plasmodium is the female Anopheles mosquito.)

Pathology-03.question: ২৬) Dog is the definitive host in following parasite:
Pathology-03.exp:
The dog is the definitive host of Echinococcus granulosus (dog tapeworm). Adult worms live in the small intestine of dogs, where they produce eggs that are passed in dog feces. Humans become accidental intermediate hosts by ingesting these eggs, leading to hydatid cyst (cystic echinococcosis) formation, mainly in the liver and lungs.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Entamoeba histolytica: Humans are the main host; causes amoebiasis.

  • Acanthamoeba: Free-living amoeba causing keratitis and encephalitis.

  • Larva migrans: Usually caused by Toxocara species; dogs and cats are definitive hosts, but the option is not a specific parasite.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Definitive host Human role
Echinococcus granulosus Dog Intermediate host (hydatid cyst)
Taenia solium Human Intermediate host → cysticercosis
Toxocara canis Dog Human → accidental host

Exam Pearl:
Dog + Echinococcus granulosus → Hydatid cyst in humans (liver/lung).

Pathology-03.question: ২৭) Parasites that are found in sputum are as follows:
Pathology-03.exp:
The larvae of Ascaris lumbricoides can be found in sputum during the pulmonary migration phase of infection. After ingestion of embryonated eggs, larvae hatch in the intestine, penetrate the intestinal wall, migrate through the bloodstream to the lungs, enter alveoli, ascend the bronchi and trachea, and are swallowed again to mature in the intestine. During this lung phase, larvae may be coughed up and detected in sputum.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Taenia solium: Eggs/proglottids are found in stool; causes taeniasis/cysticercosis.

  • Enterobius vermicularis: Eggs are found around the perianal region (cellophane tape test).

  • Balantidium coli: Trophozoites/cysts are found in stool; causes dysentery.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Specimen/Location
Ascaris larva Sputum during lung migration
Enterobius vermicularis Perianal eggs
Taenia solium Stool
Balantidium coli Stool

Exam Pearl:
Ascaris → Lung migration → Löffler syndrome → Larvae may appear in sputum.

Pathology-03.question: ২৮) Cysts found in stool are following:
Pathology-03.exp:
Entamoeba histolytica produces cysts that are found in stool and are the infective form transmitted by the fecal–oral route. Diagnosis of amoebiasis is commonly made by detecting cysts or trophozoites in stool microscopy. Mature cysts are typically quadrinucleate.

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Toxoplasma gondii: Forms tissue cysts in humans (brain, muscle), not intestinal cysts passed in stool.

  • Balantidium coli: Also produces cysts in stool, causing balantidial dysentery; however, it is not the classic answer for this question.

  • Fasciola hepatica: Eggs are found in stool, not cysts.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Stool finding
Entamoeba histolytica Cysts + trophozoites
Giardia lamblia Cysts
Balantidium coli Cysts + trophozoites
Fasciola hepatica Eggs

Exam Pearl:
E. histolytica → Stool cysts → Feco-oral transmission → Amoebic dysentery.

Pathology-03.question: ২৯) Haemoflagellates are as follows:
Pathology-03.exp:
Haemoflagellates are flagellated protozoa that are found in the blood or tissues of humans. The important human haemoflagellates are Leishmania and Trypanosoma. Among the given options, Leishmania is the correct answer.

Leishmania exists as:

  • Amastigote form → inside macrophages of humans (visceral/cutaneous leishmaniasis)

  • Promastigote form → in sandfly vector

Why other options are incorrect:

  • Trichomonas: Flagellated protozoan causing urogenital infection; not haemoflagellate.

  • Echinococcus: Cestode (tapeworm) causing hydatid cyst.

  • Plasmodium: Apicomplexan protozoan causing malaria; not a flagellate.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Parasite Group
Leishmania Haemoflagellate
Trypanosoma Haemoflagellate
Plasmodium Apicomplexa
Trichomonas Flagellated protozoa

Exam Pearl:
Haemoflagellates = Leishmania + Trypanosoma.

Pathology-03.question: ৩০) Chagas' disease is caused due to following parasite:
Pathology-03.exp: Chagas disease is caused by T. cruzi

Pathology-03.question: ৩১) Which is the infective form of E. histolytica?
Pathology-03.exp: Mature Quadrinucleate cyst is infective form of E. histolytica

Pathology-03.question: ৩২) Quartan malaria is caused by following:
Pathology-03.exp: Quartan malaria is caued by P. Malariae

Pathology-03.question: ৩৩) What is the characteristics of P. falciparum?
Pathology-03.exp: Signet ring is present in P. falciparum

Pathology-03.question: ৩৪) Which protozoa primarily infects RBC ?
Pathology-03.exp: p. falciparum infects all stages of RBC

Pathology-03.question: ৩৫) Which of the following is the haematological findings in visceral leishmaniasis?
Pathology-03.exp: Leucopenia occurs in kala-azar

Pathology-03.question: ৩৬) Amastigote form of leishmania donovani are detected in:
Pathology-03.exp: Amastigote form of leishmania donovani are detected in bone marrow aspirate

Pathology-03.question: ৩৮) Thick or Thin film are used in diagnosis of:
Pathology-03.exp:
• Diagnosis rests on microscopic examination of blood, using both thick and thin Giemsa-stained smears.
• The thick smear is used to screen for the presence of organisms, and the thin smear is used for species identification.

Pathology-03.question: ৪১) Largest intestinal nematode
Pathology-03.exp: Ascaris lumbricoides is known as the “giant roundworm.” The adults are the largest intestinal nematodes, often growing to 25 cm or more.

Pathology-03.question: ৪২) Hallmark of SLE
Pathology-03.exp: • The hallmark of SLE is the production of autoantibodies Antibodies to double-stranded DNA and the so-called Smith (Sm) antigen are virtually diagnostic of SLE.

Pathology-03.question: ৪৩) Type of hypersensitivity in SLE
Pathology-03.exp:
• The fundamental defect in SLE is a failure of the mechanisms that maintain self-tolerance.
• Most of the systemic lesions are caused by immune complexes (type III hypersensitivity).

Pathology-03.question: ৪৪) Criteria oaf arthritis in SLE excludes
Pathology-03.option4: ঘ) Joints of hands & feet are involved
Pathology-03.exp: • RA typically manifests as a symmetric arthritis principally affecting the small joints of the hand and feet.

Pathology-03.question: ৪৫) Radiographic hallmarks in RA excludes
Pathology-03.option3: গ) Widening of the joint space
Pathology-03.exp:
Radiographic hallmarks are
• Joint effusions
• Juxta-articular osteopenia with erosions
• Narrowing of the joint space
• Loss of articular cartilage

Pathology-03.question: ৪৬) Required plasma level(minimum) for development of gout
Pathology-03.exp: • Hyperuricemia (plasma urate level above 6.8 mg/dL) is necessary, but not sufficient, for the development of gout.

Pathology-03.question: ৪৭) Pathognomonic hallmark of gout
Pathology-03.exp:
• The distinctive morphologic changes in gout are
1. Acute arthritis
2. Chronic tophaceous arthritis
3. Tophi in various sites
4. Gouty nephropathy.
Tophi are the pathognomonic hallmark of gout

Pathology-03.question: ৪৮) Most common type of joint disease
Pathology-03.exp: Osteoarthritis, also called degenerative joint disease, is characterized by degeneration of cartilage that results in structural and functional failure of synovial joints. It is the most common type of joint disease.

Pathology-03.question: ৪৯) Not true about JIA
Pathology-03.option2: খ) Large joints are affected more often than small joints,
Pathology-03.option3: গ) Rheumatoid nodules and rheumatoid factor are usually present
Pathology-03.option4: ঘ) Antinuclear antibody (ANA) seropositivity is common.
Pathology-03.exp:
• Oligoarthritis is more common,
• Systemic disease is more frequent,
• Large joints are affected more often than small joints,
• Rheumatoid nodules and rheumatoid factor are usually absent, and
• Antinuclear antibody (ANA) seropositivity is common.

Pathology-03.question: ৫০) Joint spsecially aaffected in ankylosaing spondilitis
Pathology-03.exp: Ankylosing spondylitis causes destruction of articular cartilage and bony ankylosis, especially of the sacroiliac and apophyseal joints (between tuberosities and processes). It is also known as rheumatoid spondylitis and Marie- Strümpell disease. Disease involving the sacroiliac joints and vertebrae becomes symptomatic in the second and third decades of life as lower back pain and spinal immobility. Involvement of peripheral joints, such as the hips, knees, and shoulders, occurs in at least one third of affected individuals. Approximately 90% of patients are HLA-B27 positive; associations have also been found with the IL-23 receptor gene.
